title: Verifyum client receipt
description: The file `verifyum stamp` writes beside a stamped file, as <file>.verifyum.json. It holds the private draft, whose nonce is the only thing tying the file to its public proof and which Verifyum never has. A complete receipt also carries the signed proof metadata, the hourly witness bundle, the service key registry and, in version 4, the per-proof bridge into the daily checkpoint and its external-channel receipts. `verifyum verify --offline` then verifies both Merkle paths without contacting Verifyum. Written by the Python and Node clients; the two read each other's receipts.

version.description: 2 holds only the draft and proof id. 3 may carry metadata, the hourly witness_bundle and service_keys. 4 also carries witness_chain, the additive per-proof bridge from that hourly checkpoint into a daily checkpoint. Old versions remain valid.

status.description: The anchor status at the time the receipt was written. The public record is authoritative; this is a note.

private_draft.description: The half Verifyum never sees. Treat it like a key.

metadata.description: The signed public proof document, so the receipt can be checked with the operator gone.

witness_bundle.description: The Merkle path from the proof to its hourly checkpoint, and that checkpoint.

witness_chain.description: The exact hourly witness bundle plus the Merkle path from its checkpoint hash into the daily checkpoint. It contains no checkpoint member list.

service_keys.description: The Ed25519 key registry the service signature is checked against.
